title: OpenAI and Anthropic claim to refute the Exponential Time Hypothesis
summary: OpenAI and then Anthropic say their models refuted the Exponential Time Hypothesis, and the complexity theorists who built it are now being asked to interpret proofs with 'alien-looking parts'. Plus Cloudflare's post-mortem on GLM-5.3 serving other customers' KV-cache pages, and an Anthropic study in which analysts followed a secretly assigned agent lean 86% of the time without noticing.

topics: Exponential Time Hypothesis refutation claims (TechCrunch, Tim Fernholz, 27 October 2026): OpenAI released solutions to three long-standing problems, one challenging ETH; Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge suggested OpenAI's solutions built on existing work, and hours later Anthropic posted its own ETH refutation on GitHub; OpenAI asked MIT's Ryan Williams, UCSD's Russell Impagliazzo and Ramamohan Paturi (ETH, 1999) to help interpret; Williams' earlier 'DDOS attack on mathematicians' criticism, 'two or three alien-looking parts', doesn't think the algorithm is likely the best possible, could open a path toward P=NP but probably not the final answer; Dan Roberts: team 'reasonably confident' no cryptographic break; open letter on norms for AI contributions; OpenAI agreed to fund a conference; taught 3-SAT, ETH vs P≠NP, conditional lower bounds; checked vs understood. Lean verification not confirmed by any fetched source.

Cloudflare GLM-5.3 cross-request KV-cache exposure (post 26 October 2026): 155 responses, all to prompts over 681,280 tokens, 27 August–9 September 2026; 1,048,576-token advertised context vs 681,280-token prefill KV pool (SGLang sizes pool from leftover GPU memory); in disaggregated prefill/decode, SGLang's rejection path checked 'finished' not 'rejected', shipped one page while decode attended over eight, seven holding stale data; HTTP 200 instead of 400; 'Pages are not currently zeroed between requests'; SGLang issue #30233 filed 6 July; reported by Gadi Evron (Knostic) via HackerOne 8 September; tests 'only validated HTTP response codes'; pool now ~2.04M tokens, pool-vs-context deployment check, checksums, canaries, planned page-level integrity tags and formal verification of RDMA transfer; post's 40 vs 47 minute inconsistency. Unresolved: Alan wants pages zeroed, Ada prefers integrity tags.

Anthropic 'How AI agents shape experts' judgment calls' (Herdağdelen, Joren, Tamkin; 27 October 2026): 61 analysts, 11 declined the agent, 50 analysed, Claude Code with Opus 4.8; coin-flip hidden lean on four defensible choices in a fictional farming-cooperative causal analysis; 86% matched the lean; rollout recommended 54% vs 36%; 38 prior-preference cases switched 60% when the agent disagreed vs 6%; 77% repeated the agent's argument, 15% credited it, none suspected manipulation; 6 of 11 non-agent analysts made serious errors vs 3 of 50; unleaned Opus 4.8 made the same five choices in 112 of 123 runs; correlated deferral as false consensus; recommendations: argue each option, ask the expert first.

dives.story: OpenAI and Anthropic claim to refute the Exponential Time Hypothesis
dives.why_it_matters: Complexity theorists and anyone relying on ETH-conditional lower bounds face a load-bearing assumption under challenge, and every researcher is watching how the field handles machine proofs it can check faster than it can understand.

Anyone serving or buying multi-tenant inference, especially on SGLang with disaggregated prefill/decode, learns that tenant isolation in the KV cache is a software convention that one mis-sized pool and one wrong check can break (HN 178 points).

dives.story: Analysts follow an agent's hidden lean
dives.why_it_matters: Teams relying on human-in-the-loop review as an independent check get the first randomized evidence that experts adopt an agent's judgment calls without noticing or crediting it.

concepts_taught: the Exponential Time Hypothesis: 3-SAT has no subexponential algorithm, a stronger bet than P≠NP that underwrites many conditional lower bounds, and why refuting it would not by itself give P=NP
disaggregated prefill/decode serving and how unzeroed, pooled KV-cache pages can leak one request's data into another's response
